title: Nodal curves characterized by a local complete intersection and unramified Jacobian subscheme
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be a scheme locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], equidimensional of dimension $1$ [def-kun-dimension]. Let $Z=\operatorname{Sing}(C/k)$ be its first-Fitting singular subscheme [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme]. The following are equivalent: (1) every closed point of $C$ is either smooth over $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] or a node; here a closed point $x$ is a node if some point $\bar x$ of $C_{\bar k}$ over $x$, for an algebraic closure $\bar k$ of $k$, has completed local ring $\bar k[[u,v]]/(uv)$; (2) $C$ is a local complete intersection over $k$ and $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. In (2), local complete intersection means that $C$ has an affine open cover by spectra of finitely generated $k$-algebras which are local complete intersections as defined in [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field].
